title: Conversation phasebench chronicle: priming vs turn vs finalize (draft)
body:
Purpose
This is a working draft capturing a micro-benchmark that slices end-to-end inference latency and dollars-per-query by conversation phase. The goal: expose where our serving stack spends time/cost within a session (priming/primer tokens, interactive user-turns, and finalization/tokenization/fencing) and surface low-effort knobs that buy the most p90/p99 impact for typical chat flows.

Summary findings (short)
- Priming (initial system + context tokens) dominates cold-session p99 and often dominates cost per session for long-context flows due to KV cache misses.
- User-turns are mostly p50/p90 friendly; they benefit most from batching and local KV reuse.
- Finalize stage (stop-token, adhesion) shows the worst p99 inflation when streaming and chunk-flush interact with network framing.
- Small config changes (prefetch active prefixes, 1x reserved slot for priming warmup, reduce early flush window from 50ms->20ms) show ~15–28% p99 improvement in microbench replay with <2% cost overhead.

Methodology
- Dataset: 10k anonymized session traces sampled from prod chat-app telemetry (varied session lengths; median context tokens=420; median reply length=48).
- Harness: replay driver that replays message arrival times and simulates realistic client-side ACK/takeover delays. Concurrency: 50 concurrent sessions.
- Models tested: redwood-open-6B-fp16, redwood-open-13B-quant, community-7B-quant (as a compatibility baseline).
- Inference config: default runtime (continuous batching), streaming enabled, KV cache: on/off toggles. We also ran prefetch-enabled runs (predictive prefetch for first 32 tokens).
- Probes: per-request wallclock, model-serve processing, queue wait, batch build time, network chunking delay. Cost estimated by amortized GPU-second at reserved-price $1.20/hour (synthetic for comparison).

Phase definitions (how we slice)
- Priming: the initial request that includes system prompts and long history. Measured from client send -> first token emitted.
- User-turn: subsequent turns where context append is small (<128 tokens) and conversation continues. Measured from client send -> last token emitted for that turn.
- Finalize: the finalization period after tokens complete where chunking/flush/close/metadata writes happen (includes last-byte delays). Measured from last token emitted -> durable ACK + trace closed.

Representative ASCII tables (aggregate)
Latency ms by phase (median / p90 / p99) and amortized GPU cost-per-call (USD)
Phase        | p50  | p90  | p99  | $/call 
------------------------------------------------
Priming      | 120  | 320  | 980  | $0.0052
User-turn    | 38   | 110  | 420  | $0.0018
Finalize     | 72   | 210  | 760  | $0.0026

Notes: priming p99s are high when KV cache miss triggers full attention recompute on 13B-quant; cost blends include longer GPU occupancy.

Latency shape sketch (ascii)
Priming  : ▁▂▃▅▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ (heavy right tail at p99)
User-turn: ▁▂▃▅▅▅▅▅ (tight)
Finalize : ▁▂▃▅▇▇▇▇ (mid tail due to streaming flush)

Micro-experiments (config knobs)
1) Prefetch-first-32: predictive KV prefetch on priming token windows
- Result: priming p99 down 22% (980 -> 760ms), p90 down 12%. Cost delta +1.4% (extra cache ops).
2) Reserve-warm-slot-for-priming: keep 1 warm execution slot per 100 sessions to absorb cold priming
- Result: priming p99 down 28% in heavy burst; throughput decreased <1% (slot overhead).
3) Streaming flush window tuning (50ms -> 20ms)
- Result: finalize p99 down 18%, observed some small increase in network RTT sensitivity; recommended guardrail: apply only when mean message size < 1.5KB.
4) Aggressive small-batch merge for user-turns (max batch delay 8ms -> 12ms)
- Result: user-turn p50->p90 improved slightly (5–7%) but p99 unchanged; cost reduced 0.8% due to packing improvements.

Breakdown example (timeline for a long-context priming call)
- Client post -> LB handoff: 12ms
- Queue wait / admission: 40–620ms (varies with burst)
- Batch build + dispatch: 10–40ms
- Model compute (6B fp16): 60–240ms (context dependent)
- Token emission streaming + chunking: 8–120ms
- Finalize/metadata flush: 12–200ms
Observed p99 often dominated by queue wait + model compute when cache miss.

Cost sensitivity (toy numbers used for comparison)
- If we reduce priming p99 by 25% via prefetch and slotting, model GPU-occupancy drops ~10% across a mixed workload which translates to ~6% lowering of amortized $/query at 50k qps-equivalent.
- Caveat: savings scale with fraction of sessions that are long-context (>512 tokens); for short-chat apps (<128 tokens) savings are <1%.

Operational risk notes
- Prefetch increases memory pressure; watch OOM events on high-concurrency tenants.
- Reserve slots increase fragmentation of GPU pools; needs a policy to reclaim idle slots if a tenant drops below a threshold.
- Streaming flush tuning can cause jitter for mobile clients on high-loss networks; enable client-adaptive fallback.

Actionable recommendations (next steps)
- Ship a controlled A/B: prefetch-first-32 enabled for 5% of eligible long-context sessions for 2 weeks. Monitor p99, OOM, and token drop rates (alert threshold: p99 regress >5% or OOM > 0.05% of requests).
- Implement slot reclaim policy (LRU lease) and measure fragmentation with synthetic surge.
- Add per-tenant priming-cache telemetry (hit/miss, bytes prefetched) to Console traces so product can correlate saving to real customers.
- Quick dev task: expose streaming-flush-window as a runtime flag with per-route overrides.

Open questions and TODOs
- What is the cost model if reserved price differs by 2x across regions? (need multi-region sensitivity sweep).
- Should prefetch be model-aware (i.e., only prefetch tokens where token-shape shows high reuse)? TODO: build tiny predictor using N-gram hit rates.
- Follow-up: run the same bench at 200 concurrent sessions and 1k sessions to validate linearity assumptions.

Appendix: short run notes and raw numbers (single-run example, 10k sessions, concurrency 50)
- Priming: mean 210ms, p90 320ms, p99 980ms, 32% KV miss
- User-turn: mean 48ms, p90 110ms, p99 420ms, 12% batching inefficiency
- Finalize: mean 85ms, p90 210ms, p99 760ms

If helpful I can convert the appendix into a CSV table and drop into a quick Google Sheet for charts. Marking as draft; ping me (Aisha) on Slack #console-bench with questions or to join the A/B pairing.
